clue.text: Material in carol needs a bit of learning

indicators.note: in places the word for material inside the word for carol, splitting it open

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
matter is physical material or substance

explanation.surface: A request that the stuff in a Christmas song should carry some educational content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cloth in a carol singer's costume, but it means physical substance; 'in' is the container signal and 'needs' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, superficial knowledge of a subject is only a sprinkling of what there is to know.

clue.text: Get money for some counselling

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word counselling is taken, a run from its middle

explanation.surface: A counsellor wondering how to be paid for their sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade goods away is to receive payment in exchange for them.

clue.text: It helps one look you in the eye, when giving you the news

definitions.text: It helps one look you in the eye, when giving you the news

parts.words: It helps one look you in the eye, when giving you the news
parts.note: a newsreader seems to meet the viewer's gaze because the script scrolls on a screen in front of the camera lens

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like praise for a newsreader's candour, but it describes the prompting device fixed to the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A television prompter shows the script on glass over the lens, so a presenter can read while seeming to look straight at viewers.

clue.text: Try undeniable criminal, but condone offence

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of try undeniable are wrongly arranged and must be put right

explanation.surface: Advice to a lenient judge: put the obviously guilty on trial, yet let the crime pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' sits naturally beside 'undeniable' as an adjective but signals the anagram of TRY UNDENIABLE; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend not to see wrongdoing is to excuse or overlook it, an idiom from Nelson ignoring a signal.

clue.text: Gave up work, accepting the inevitable

definitions.meaning: left a job formally, as by handing in notice
reluctantly reconciled to something that cannot be changed

explanation.surface: Someone quitting their job because there was nothing else to be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting a post and being passively reconciled to fate are both senses of stepping down or submitting.

clue.text: Nigel finally moves to other side of river

indicators.note: the final letter of the name Nigel, L for left, is swapped for its opposite side, R for right

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel ends up crossing a river to the far bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Nigel crossing over; in fact his last letter L (left) becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a major river of West Africa, flowing through Mali and Nigeria.

clue.text: Put up with a nuisance

definitions.meaning: tolerated, in the past tense, as in endured a burden
a tedious or irritating person or thing

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating an irritating companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of bear means tolerated, and the noun is a dull, tiresome person or thing.

clue.text: Nothing to confine thought

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O
to pinion is to bind someone's arms and so restrain them

explanation.surface: A claim that there is nothing that can contain a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or belief held about something is what a person thinks of it.

clue.text: Mark, say, is leaving set confused

indicators.note: confused tells the solver the letters of leaving set are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark walking off a film set in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name in a story about leaving a set; it is St Mark, author of a Gospel. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: St Mark is one of the four Gospel writers, so he is an example of such a preacher of the Christian message.

clue.text: Not yet? Dead right

parts.note: the late so-and-so is someone who has died

explanation.surface: An impatient question answered with a grim confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' reads as a phrase meaning quite correct, but splits into LATE (dead) and R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Something that will happen afterwards, at a future time, has not happened yet.

clue.text: Miss Italy?

parts.note: reads as a beauty-contest title, but asks for the Italian word used to address an unmarried young woman

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'Miss Italy' is not a beauty queen but what a miss is called in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian form of address for an unmarried young woman corresponds to the English title Miss.

clue.text: May he seek a hobby? He has one already

definitions.text: May he seek a hobby? He has one already

parts.words: May he seek a hobby? He has one already
parts.note: a hobby is also a small falcon, so a birdwatcher may seek one while already having a pastime

explanation.walkthrough: A hobby is a small falcon as well as a pastime, so a birdwatcher hunts for one while already having one.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of birds may go looking for a falcon called the hobby, and bird study is itself a pastime.

clue.text: Getting those that are cast to speak in every possible way

definitions.text: Getting those that are cast to speak in every possible way

parts.words: Getting those that are cast to speak in every possible way
parts.note: bells are cast in a foundry, and ringers sound them through every possible sequence

explanation.walkthrough: 'those that are cast' sounds like actors, but means bells, cast in metal; making them 'speak' in every order is the English art of ringing permutations.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of bell-ringing works through mathematical permutations of a set of tuned bells, sounding them in every possible order.

clue.text: Motionless, like farm animals?

definitions.meaning: completely still, not moving at all
livestock that are still, read whimsically as a description of cattle

explanation.surface: Cattle standing frozen in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly unmoving, with a pun on stock meaning farm livestock that keep quite still.

clue.text: Type of music boat race crew would like?

definitions.text: Type of music boat race crew would like?

parts.words: Type of music boat race crew would like?
parts.note: the Oxford and Cambridge rowers are awarded Blues, so they would enjoy a melancholy style of music named for them

explanation.walkthrough: In the Boat Race (an annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames) the oarsmen win Blues, sporting colours, hence the music they would favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A melancholic African-American musical genre shares its name with the colours awarded to Oxbridge sportsmen.

clue.text: Type of music to make an alto struggle?

indicators.note: struggle suggests the letters of an alto are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Music without a key that would trouble a contralto singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' acts on AN ALTO, giving its anagram; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written without a key or tonal centre is described as lacking tonality.

clue.text: Spanish town where girl receives amazing tan

indicators.note: receives means the girl's name takes another piece inside it
amazing suggests the letters of tan are astonishingly scrambled

explanation.surface: A girl on holiday in a Spanish resort acquiring a remarkable suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' looks like praise for the suntan but is the anagram signal on 'tan', and 'receives' puts the result inside the girl's name; 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port and resort city on Spain's Costa Blanca.

clue.text: Nefariously inspecting the cladding

definitions.meaning: scouting a place before a robbery, as in reconnoitring a joint
a protective outer cover or shell

explanation.surface: A burglar surveying a building's exterior covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal slang for checking out premises before a theft, and an enclosing outer layer or covering.

clue.text: Hired killer or what he uses

definitions.meaning: slang for a gun, the weapon such a killer carries

explanation.surface: An assassin and his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman is a hitman, and the same slang word names the pistol he fires.

clue.text: Slips and other underwear

definitions.meaning: baggy knickers, a different undergarment from a slip

explanation.surface: A drawer of petticoats and other undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' seems to be petticoats, which makes 'other underwear' natural; in fact it means mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunders are howlers in British slang, and long loose knickers are a women's undergarment.

clue.text: Flags, sensing sickness

indicators.note: sickness suggests the letters of sensing are disordered, put in an unhealthy jumble

explanation.surface: Banners that seem to detect illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval or national banners flown from ships are flags of this kind.

clue.text: The two censors in error? Goodness me!

indicators.note: in error means the letters of the two censors are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of censors making a blunder, met with an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A British exclamation of astonishment, like gosh or well I never.

clue.text: Store oxygen in solid form

indicators.note: in places the oxygen symbol inside the word for solid

parts.note: something in solid form is hard, not soft or liquid
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Keeping oxygen frozen into a solid state.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile or hidden cache is a stock that has been put away.

clue.text: Cause trouble in prison

explanation.surface: An inmate stirring up unrest behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke trouble is to stir things up, and the same word is British slang for jail.

clue.text: At sea, for the most part

definitions.meaning: out on the open ocean, the main being an old word for the sea

explanation.surface: A sailor saying where they spend most of their time.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the ocean, and the phrase also means mostly or generally.

clue.text: A very expensive bar

parts.note: sounds like a pricey pub, but means a cast block of precious metal such as gold

explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub with steep prices; it is a solid bar of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A block of cast gold or other precious metal is a bar worth a great deal.

clue.text: Fat boy crosses river

indicators.note: the boy crosses the river by straddling it, so his word goes around the river's letter

explanation.surface: A lad wading across a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig fat rendered for cooking is a kind of edible fat.

clue.text: His notice may appear in newspaper column

definitions.text: His notice may appear in newspaper column

parts.words: His notice may appear in newspaper column
parts.note: a person promoting goods pays for a notice to be printed in the paper's columns

explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' suggests a review of someone's work, but it is a paid announcement, and the man is the one who placed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pays to promote goods publicly places notices in newspapers.
